title: A Conference Programme
summary: Read a fictional management conference schedule, then practise finding details, understanding statements and completing information.
sourceNote: Original practice exercise inspired by the conference-programme reading task format.
passage:
NORTHSTAR LEADERSHIP CONFERENCE

Venue: Riverside Conference Centre
Date: 18 June

MORNING PROGRAMME

9.00–9.20 | Welcome and opening remarks
Speaker: Daniel Reed
An introduction to the day and its main themes.

9.20–10.30 | Building a supportive team
Speaker: Sofia Nguyen
Explore practical ways to help team members feel included and work well together.

10.30–11.00 | Coffee break

11.00–12.15 | Communicating across cultures
Speaker: Lucas Pereira
Learn how communication styles can differ and how to avoid misunderstandings in international teams.

12.15–1.30 | Lunch

AFTERNOON PROGRAMME

1.30–2.45 | Planning a successful project
Speaker: Aisha Khan
Discover how to set clear goals, share responsibilities and keep a project on schedule.

2.45–3.00 | Short break

3.00–4.00 | Creative problem-solving workshop
Speaker: Ethan Brooks
Work in small groups to explore different solutions to workplace challenges.

4.00–4.30 | Closing session
Speaker: Daniel Reed
A summary of the main ideas and final questions.

title: The Bicycle Path Behind the River
summary: A short passage about a new bicycle path in Mapleford, with short-answer, sentence-completion and True/False/Not Given questions.
passage:
Last year, the town of Mapleford opened a new bicycle path behind the river. The path is three kilometres long and connects the train station with the sports centre. Before the path was built, cyclists had to use a busy road with many cars.

The new path is popular with students because it passes near two schools. It is also used by office workers who want a quiet route in the morning. The town council added lights along the path, so people can use it safely in the early evening.

There are still some problems. After heavy rain, water collects near the middle of the path. The council plans to improve drainage in July. Some residents have also asked for more rubbish bins because snack wrappers are sometimes left near the benches.

title: A New Use for Old Buildings
summary: A passage about reusing old buildings, with matching information, summary completion and multiple-choice questions.
passage:
A  Many towns have old buildings that are no longer used for their original purpose. A factory may close, a cinema may lose its audience, or a railway station may become unnecessary after a new line is built. Instead of knocking these buildings down, some towns are giving them a second life.

B  One reason is cost. Building something completely new can be expensive. If the walls and roof of an old building are still strong, it may be cheaper to repair the inside. Reuse can also save materials, which is better for the environment.

C  Old buildings often carry local memories. A former cinema may remind residents of childhood weekends, while an old station may represent the town’s connection with other places. When these buildings are reused, the town keeps part of its history.

D  However, reuse is not always simple. Some old buildings have narrow doors, weak floors or poor heating. They may need major changes before people can use them safely. Designers must also decide which old features to keep and which to replace.

E  Successful projects often mix old and new. In one town, an old factory became an art school. The brick walls were kept, but large windows were added to bring in more light. Students said the building felt creative because it did not look like a normal classroom.

questions.question: 1. Which paragraph gives examples of original purposes that may disappear? (Write A–E)
questions.explanation: Đoạn A nêu factory, cinema và railway station có thể mất chức năng ban đầu.

questions.question: 2. Which paragraph gives a reason why reuse can be environmentally helpful? (Write A–E)
questions.explanation: Đoạn B nói việc tái sử dụng có thể tiết kiệm vật liệu, tốt hơn cho môi trường.

questions.question: 3. Which paragraph describes emotional value connected to old buildings? (Write A–E)
questions.explanation: Đoạn C nói về local memories, childhood weekends và lịch sử của thị trấn.

questions.question: 4. Which paragraph describes physical problems that may make reuse difficult? (Write A–E)
questions.explanation: Đoạn D nêu narrow doors, weak floors và poor heating.

questions.question: 5. Which paragraph gives an example of a building changed into a place for learning? (Write A–E)
questions.explanation: Đoạn E kể một nhà máy cũ được chuyển thành art school.

questions.question: 6. Which paragraph mentions a design change that increased natural light? (Write A–E)
questions.explanation: Đoạn E nói large windows were added to bring in more light.

questions.question: 7. Reusing old buildings can be cheaper than constructing something new if the ______ and roof are still strong. (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS)
questions.explanation: Đoạn B: “If the walls and roof of an old building are still strong...”

questions.question: 8. Reuse can also save ______. (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS)
questions.explanation: Đoạn B: “Reuse can also save materials.”

questions.question: 9. Old buildings may contain local ______. (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS)
questions.explanation: Đoạn C: “Old buildings often carry local memories.”

questions.question: 10. Some old buildings need major changes before they are ______. (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS)
questions.explanation: Đoạn D viết “before people can use them safely”; câu tóm tắt dùng tính từ safe.

questions.question: 11. What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Old buildings can sometimes be reused in valuable ways.
All old buildings should become railway stations.
New buildings are always cheaper than old ones.
Towns should remove all old cinemas.
questions.answer: Old buildings can sometimes be reused in valuable ways.
questions.explanation: Toàn bài nêu lợi ích, giá trị, khó khăn và ví dụ về việc tái sử dụng công trình cũ.

questions.question: 12. Why were large windows added to the old factory?
options: To make the building colder
To bring in more light
To hide the brick walls
To stop students entering
questions.explanation: Đoạn E: “large windows were added to bring in more light.”

questions.question: 13. According to the passage, designers need to decide ______.
options: which old features to keep or replace
how to close every old factory
which students should study art
how to build a new railway line
questions.answer: which old features to keep or replace
questions.explanation: Đoạn D nói designers phải quyết định giữ lại hay thay thế những đặc điểm cũ nào.

answerInstructions: Questions 1–6: Write A–E. Questions 7–10: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Questions 11–13: Choose A, B, C or D.

title: Learning in Public Libraries
summary: A passage about the changing role of public libraries, with matching headings, Yes/No/Not Given, table completion and short-answer questions.
sourceNote: Based on the learning passage and answer explanations supplied by the user.
passage:
A  Public libraries used to be seen mainly as places for borrowing books. That role is still important, but many libraries now support a wider range of learning. Visitors may attend workshops, use computers, join reading groups or receive help with forms and online services.

B  This change is partly a response to digital life. Many everyday tasks, from applying for jobs to booking medical appointments, now require internet access. People without a computer at home can easily feel excluded. In my opinion, libraries are one of the fairest places to offer digital support because they are open to everyone.

C  Libraries also provide a calm study environment. Not every student has a quiet desk at home. Some live in crowded flats, while others share rooms with younger siblings. A library table, even for one hour, can give a learner the space needed to focus.

D  Another important service is community teaching. In some libraries, volunteers teach older adults how to send emails or use video calls. In others, parents learn how to read with young children. These classes are usually simple, but they can have a strong effect on daily life.

E  The challenge is funding. New services need trained staff, working computers and safe spaces. If libraries are expected to do more without extra support, the quality of service may fall. A modern library should not be treated as a free solution to every social problem, but it can be a powerful starting point.
